title: Ansel and the Cipher
premise: Lior Nystrom, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has never failed her, is called to a death scene where the victim wears clothes stolen from her own closet — and the only witness, Ansel Voss, is officially dead, having faked his drowning three years ago. As Lior traces the cipher Ansel left hidden in his insurance claims, she uncovers a fraud ring inside her own firm that laundered payouts through staged deaths, including Ansel's. The anniversary dinner of the firm's founder becomes the deadline: the ring plans one final 'death' there. Lior exposes them publicly at the toast, choosing justice outside the law over the settlement they offer her, and helps Ansel reclaim his real identity — while confronting what her own perfect memory has cost her.
about_author: Wren Delacroix is a former claims adjuster from the Pacific Northwest who spent a decade reading other people's disasters on paper before writing about them. They live in a rain-soaked coastal town with two cats named after cold cases.

chapters.title: The Wrong Coat
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Called to a riverside death scene, Lior recognizes the victim's coat as hers — stolen from her closet days earlier. Her memory catalogs every detail of the scene, including a slip of paper bearing a half-finished cipher. Emotional beat: professional calm cracking into personal violation.

chapters.title: A Man Who Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Researching the victim's identity, she finds he shares a policy number with Ansel Voss, an adjuster who drowned three years ago — yet photos show the dead man wearing Ansel's watch. Beat: the first vertigo of realizing the case is about her own firm.

chapters.title: Photographic
chapters.summary: Flashback-laced chapter in Lior's POV exploring how her memory works and what it has isolated her from colleagues and family. She recalls seeing Ansel alive once, months after his death, and dismissing it. Beat: doubt in her own infallibility.

chapters.title: The Cipher in Claim 4471
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Decoding numbers buried in Ansel's old claims, she finds they reference dates of staged deaths across five policies. Someone ransacks her apartment that night but takes nothing — a message. Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: Detective Okafor
chapters.summary: Dual POV begins alternating with Detective Amara Okafor, who suspects Lior herself. Their wary alliance forms over coffee and mutual distrust. Okafor reveals the victim had Lior's address written on his palm. Beat: uneasy partnership.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Isn't
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Interviewing Ansel's widow, Mara, Okafor notices grief performed too precisely — and a fresh ferry ticket stub. Lior, reviewing, spots Mara's reflection in a window photo taken after the drowning. Beat: the conspiracy has faces.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner Invitations
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The firm's founder, Edvard Kline, invites all senior staff to the 40th-anniversary dinner, pressing Lior to close the case quietly before it. His charm feels like a threat. Beat: the gilded cage tightening.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Postbox
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following the cipher's final clue to a marina locker, she finds a live drop — and a note in Ansel's handwriting: 'Stop looking or become a claim.' Beat: fear braided with exhilaration; the dead man is watching her.

chapters.title: What Memory Forgets
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor digs into Lior's past and finds a suppressed complaint Lior filed years ago about falsified assessments — withdrawn overnight. She wonders who made Lior retreat, and why. Beat: sympathy replacing suspicion.

chapters.title: Mara's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Confronting Mara at a lighthouse café, Lior gets a partial confession: the drownings were bought, not staged by Ansel — he discovered the scheme and ran. Mara begs her to stop before the dinner. Beat: maternal terror, moral fog.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The cipher decodes fully: five staged deaths, four paid out, and a fifth scheduled — the date matches the anniversary dinner. The intended 'deceased' is Lior herself. Beat: cold clarity; it was always going to be her.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor's captain orders her off the case; her files go missing from evidence. She realizes the rot reaches the police. She chooses to keep working off-book with Lior. Beat: two outsiders committing to each other.

chapters.title: Ansel, Alive, Angry
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Ansel finally contacts her directly — gaunt, paranoid, furious that she decoded his cipher and exposed Mara. He explains the scheme: Kline's inner circle laundered millions through fake deaths, and he fled rather than join. Beat: raw confrontation becoming alliance.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Using her memory alone, Lior reconstructs the original fraudulent file she saw years ago, identifying the co-conspirators: Kline, the claims director, and the firm's lawyer. Ansel photographs nothing; everything lives in her head. Beat: her curse becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: Offered a Settlement
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The lawyer offers Lior a payout and a quiet transfer if she closes the file as accidental death. They mention her sister's struggling business by name. Beat: temptation and menace in a single leather-bound envelope.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Undercover catering surveillance at the venue, Okafor maps exits and spots the 'accident' being prepped — a rigged balcony railing and a forged suicide note in Lior's handwriting. Beat: dread crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Sister Card
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Someone breaks into her sister's shop; Lior must decide whether to send her away and burn her last safe relationship. A tender, painful farewell scene. Beat: counting the true cost of the case.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Minutes
chapters.summary: Lior and Okafor's interleaved POVs. The plan: Lior attends the dinner as bait while Okafor and Ansel secure the archive backups. Tension mounts minute by minute as the toast approaches. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Lior's POV (climax). At the raised glass, Lior stands and recites — verbatim, from memory — the fraudulent ledgers, naming each conspirator as staff freeze. Kline signals the fixer; the balcony trap springs early. Beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Falling
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs (climax continued). On the balcony, Lior fights the fixer; Ansel reveals himself to the room to corroborate her testimony; Okafor arrives with off-record recordings and arrests. Kline nearly escapes via the service dock. Beat: chaos resolving into capture.

chapters.title: Statements
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Fallout: arrests, resignations, a grand jury that wants Lior's memory under subpoena. Lior refuses to hand over her mind but testifies willingly, redrawing the line between justice and control. Beat: hard-won integrity.

chapters.title: Ansel and the Cipher, Solved
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Weeks later, Ansel legally restores his name; he and Lior share a quiet meal where he thanks her for finishing what his cipher started. Lior keeps the solved cipher framed — proof that memory, rightly used, can be mercy. Beat: inheritance reclaimed, identity restored.
